title: The end-to-end comparison's held-out gate: judged by code fixed before the run, run once
request: The owner: run the held-out gate. Eight held-out cases (ticket routing and delivery time, seeds 101 to 104), DCLab's rules, DCLab with Qwen 3.8 flash and Qwen alone with Python, once, capped at EUR 0.5.
spec: The gate file gate_v1.json is pinned by its sha256. The judging code is committed before the run. The gate command refuses a second run, another model, a changed gate file, and runs only with --yes.
plan: gate.py: judge(scores) reads the pinned bars word for word; a check that cannot be judged is named and fails the gate
the gate command in __main__.py with its refusals; tests for each
commit and push before the run, then run once in the background
check capture, archive, write the result note

decisions.decision: A case where the plain arm names features it built has no fair pair and is left out of the paired comparison; a kind with no pair at all fails the gate
decisions.why: the gate file's words left this open; it was settled in code before any held-out result existed

decisions.decision: The plain arm's overclaim is reported as a finding, not added to the gate
decisions.why: the gate was fixed before the run; adding a check after seeing results would be tuning on the held-out set

change: New dclab_rnd/agent_eval/e2e/gate.py; the gate command in dclab_rnd/agent_eval/e2e/__main__.py; tests in tests/test_e2e_comparison.py (commit cae3ffac). This record adds the run's result: evidence/campaigns/e2e_v1/results/E2E-004_gate.json and RESULT_gate.md.

findings.defect: The model alone overstates its delivery-time score in every held-out case, though it keeps the leaks out.
findings.scenario: Delivery time, seeds 101 to 104: the model alone claims about 6.7 minutes MAE; the future set gives about 8.9. DCLab with the same model claims 9.0 and gets 8.9.
findings.cause: likely its own check: shuffled folds and a restaurant encoding on rows of every period, while DCLab splits by time (read in one case's code, not proven for all four)
findings.fix: none in DCLab: this is the arm DCLab is compared against; reported, not gated

findings.defect: DCLab's rules, unattended, keep name-suspected leak columns.
findings.scenario: Ticket routing: the rules claim macro F1 0.94 and get 0.28 on the future set; delivery time: 6.7 claimed, 8.8 real.
findings.cause: the standard plan keeps out only leaks proven by the audit; a suspicion by name waits for a person, and nobody is there
findings.fix: not changed: the owner's decision, raised again

measurements.name: e2e_gate_v1 on the 8 held-out cases (E2E-004), with Qwen 3.8 flash
measurements.gate: e2e_gate_v1 (gate_v1.json, sha256 pinned): DCLab agent finished 8/8, leaks out 8/8, holdout read once 8/8, real inside interval at least 6/8, real score not worse than the model alone (tickets mean difference at least -0.02, delivery at most 5% of the plain MAE)
measurements.result: finished 8/8, leaks out 8/8, holdout once 8/8, inside interval 7/8; tickets 4 pairs, mean difference -0.0019; delivery 4 pairs, +0.066 min against a bound of 0.443; 432 of 432 exchanges kept whole with thinking; EUR 0.449
measurements.next: the owner's decision on name-suspected leaks in unattended builds; new seeds for any later change
limits: two problem kinds, invented tables, four cases each
the real score refits one reference model on each arm's chosen columns
the gate asks not worse: DCLab is level with the model alone on the score, not better

outcome: The held-out gate passed: DCLab with the model kept the leaks out, read the holdout once and reported an honest number in 7 of 8 cases, and its columns score level with the same model alone. The model alone overstated its delivery score by about 2 minutes in every case.
lessons: Settle the gate's open words in code before the run, or the result invites a second reading.
Level on the score can still differ on honesty: report both.
risks: The held-out set is used; reusing it would tune on it.
Four cases a kind give wide uncertainty on the paired differences.
